players.product: superconducting QPUs made in its own Fab-1 (84-qubit Ankaa-3 on Amazon Braket, 36-qubit Cepheus-1-36Q chiplet system, 9-qubit Novera on-premises QPU)

quarterly_data.signal: Rigetti 8-K: on September 4, 2026 Rigetti's subsidiary signed an Other Transaction Agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce for up to $100 million of CHIPS Act funding to accelerate superconducting quantum computing R&D - $43.9 million available at or soon after the award date and two milestone tranches of $29.9 million and $26.2 million - for three projects: compressing readout electronics into an integrated miniaturized package, expanding cryogenic capacity by orders of magnitude with a new cryostat architecture, and developing fabrication capabilities for high-connectivity chip architectures; the Department receives a minority, non-controlling equity stake. CEO Subodh Kulkarni: 'Shortening the time to build quantum systems at scale and reducing their cost will also allow for broader adoption.'
quarterly_data.figure: up to $100 million; $43.9 million; $29.9 million; $26.2 million
